summary: Hosted canary rollout auto-paused unexpectedly after brief p95 latency spike (beta customer)
description:
Customer reports their Hosted canary rollout auto-paused at the 25% step immediately after a short latency spike, despite overall application health appearing normal. They want to understand why it paused, whether this indicates a canary regression, and how to tune/avoid false positives during beta.

Issue summary
- What: Rollout transitioned to AUTO_PAUSED with reason "p95 latency regression > threshold".
- When: 2025-03-27 ~18:10–18:25 UTC during step 25%.
- Where: prod/us-east, route: /v1/chat/completions (Northstar customer route alias: support-agent-prod).
- Impact: Rollout progression blocked; customer held at 25% canary traffic for ~45 minutes until manual action. No hard outage, but rollout confidence reduced.

Customer-reported symptoms
- Console showed: "Rollout paused automatically due to SLO breach".
- Customer observed: brief latency increase across their app; no material increase in 5xx; canary model did not appear uniquely affected.

Expected behavior
- Auto-pause/rollback should trigger when canary cohort is reliably worse than baseline beyond configured thresholds, not when both baseline and canary are affected by a transient regional issue.

Actual behavior
- Auto-pause triggered on a short p95 spike; cohort comparison logic flagged canary regression even though baseline p95 also spiked in the same window.

Initial hypothesis
- Threshold sensitivity + evaluation window too short at 25% traffic created a false positive under transient regional latency. Also possible that the comparison job sampled unevenly across cohorts during the spike.

Notes
- This ticket is part of Hosted canary rollouts beta feedback. Customer asked for recommended settings (min soak time / evaluation window / sample size) and whether thresholds are configurable per route.

resolution:
Determined auto-pause was a false positive triggered by default p95 latency regression rule during a transient us-east latency incident affecting both cohorts, combined with a short evaluation window and low/uneven sample sizes immediately after a step change. Customer resumed rollout after the event cleared and completed rollout successfully.

Customer-facing outcome
- Provided explanation with timestamps + cohort dashboard interpretation.
- Recommended threshold tuning (longer lookback, higher regression threshold temporarily, minimum sample-size gating) for subsequent rollouts.

Internal outcome
- Captured beta feedback to adjust recommended wizard defaults and to add safeguards (sample size + grace period after step transitions) to reduce false pauses.
